headline: Julia Lee sees Australian bank margins pressured as rate hike cycle ends while competition intensifies
reasoning: Julia Lee notes that rising interest rates have been a positive for bank net interest margins, but intensifying competition has been a negative headwind. She argues Australia is near the end of its rate hiking cycle, so banks won't see much more of a 'sugar hit' from higher rates. Meanwhile, competition is not going away in a quarter and will continue to weigh on margins. She also highlights falling mortgage applications across the big four, with Westpac down 20%, NAB and CBA down 15%, and ANZ the best at down 12%.
quote: I think this reporting season hearing from the big four banks, what we have seen is that rising interest rates have been good news for the net interest margin. But then on the flip side, intensifying competition has been bad news. So one's been positive and one's been negative. The problem is that we're probably at the end of that interest hiking cycle here in Australia or near the end. So you're not going to see much more of a sugar hit for the banks coming through from rising interest rates, because we're pretty much almost there. Um, but on the flip side, intensifying competition's not going to go away in a quarter. That's going to continue to have an impact.
episode_title: Switzer| Ryan Stokes goes deep on markets

headline: Julia Lee observes rotation into Australian mid-caps as big bank headwinds drive broadening of market leadership

She suggests that if banks remain out of favour, smaller and mid-cap companies that benefit from near-peak interest rates could attract flows. Sectors she highlights as benefiting include technology, healthcare (which has been beaten up), energy and materials.
quote: We have seen a bit of a rotation into the mid caps this month where we have seen some outperformance coming through.
